newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: ACI says Jan-Oct 1996 world air cargo up 5.9 pct.
newsitem.headline: ACI says Jan-Oct 1996 world air cargo up 5.9 pct.

text.p: Freight and mail traffic handled by 478 airports around the world between January and October 1996, totalled 40.46 million tonnes, up 5.9 percent on the same period the previous year, said Geneva-based Airports Council International (ACI).
North America, the biggest of ACI's six cargo-handling regions, reported 21.36 million tonnes of freight traffic, up 6.6 percent on January-October 1995.

Airports in the Asia/Pacific region (in which ACI incorporates Indo-China, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Thailand, Japan, Malaysia and Australia), tabled cargo throughput of 8.31 million tonnes, an increase of 5.4 percent on the first ten months of last year, ACI said.
January-October 1996 cargo traffic handled at ACI's Europe member airports totalled 8.30 million tonnes, a rise of 4.1 percent on the same period in 1995.
Middle East airports recorded the highest growth rate of ACI's cargo-handling regions in the period in question, throughput rising 16.6 percent to 1.13 million tonnes.
Freight throughput at Latin America/Caribbrean airports was up 0.2 percent on January-October 1995 levels at 999,620 tonnes.
African airports cargo traffic improved by 6.7 percent on the first ten months of 1995 to 358,077 tonnes. -- Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
